patch.value: A sandboxed fixture records provenance from the host harness environment, so the suite is green on CI and deterministically red for any agent running it locally

A sandboxed test fixture that simulates one harness records provenance derived from the environment of whatever harness is running the test process, so the suite's verdict is a function of the developer's machine rather than of the fixture.

Reproduced deterministically at commit 9a0a048b6, twice, once under a full coverage run and once in isolation. The failing test is tests/unit/sdk/agent-runtime-primitives.spec.ts, attributes update and close mutations to the detected harness. It constructs a simulated codex actor and asserts the exact shape of the two history entries that result. On this machine both entries carry an extra context block, agent_provenance_outcomes.version, with status failed, reason resolver_failed, resolver ai_agent_version and rule_version v1. The assertion compares whole entries, so the unexpected block fails it. With the single environment variable AI_AGENT removed the same spec passes sixteen of sixteen. That is the whole difference.

The mechanism is a three-step leak and every step is ordinary. The codex harness descriptor at src/core/shared/author.ts:219 declares provenance_resolvers with version mapped to ai_agent_version. The resolver at src/core/shared/author.ts:569 reads env.AI_AGENT and matches a version anchored at the end of the string. The outcome classifier at src/core/shared/author.ts:897 decides between failed and unavailable by asking only whether env.AI_AGENT is non-blank, not whether the value belongs to the harness the descriptor matched.

So on a hosted runner AI_AGENT is unset, the classifier reports unavailable with reason harness_unavailable, and the expectation holds. On the machine of an agent running the suite locally AI_AGENT is set by that agent's own harness. Here it is claude-code_2-1-226_agent, which ends in the literal text agent rather than a version, so the regex does not match, the resolver returns nothing, and because the variable was nevertheless present the classifier upgrades the outcome from unavailable to failed and stamps resolver_failed into the record. A simulated codex actor's immutable history entry therefore carries a diagnostic about the real Claude Code process that ran the test.

The first consequence is a local and hosted divergence with the wrong polarity, and it lands on precisely the audience this project exists to serve. Continuous integration is green at this commit. Any coding agent that runs the documented local command sees a deterministic red suite, and both harnesses this project targets set AI_AGENT. Local verification is meant to be at least as strict as hosted verification so that a green local run predicts a green push. Here it is differently strict rather than more strict: it fails on something hosted cannot observe while hosted passes on something local cannot reach. A contributor meeting this has no signal distinguishing it from a real regression, and the natural response, re-running or assuming a flake, is wrong in both directions.

The second consequence is the deeper one and is about the product rather than the suite. The sandbox does not isolate harness provenance. withTempPmPath redirects PM_PATH and PM_GLOBAL_PATH and neutralizes telemetry, so storage is contained, but the harness signal environment passes straight through. Any recorded provenance produced inside a sandbox is therefore a function of the host. For an outcome milestone whose claim is provable history, a field of the record that varies with who ran the process is a containment breach rather than a flaky assertion, and it is the same class of defeat that reproducible byte-identical workspace construction was built to rule out: two hosts constructing the same fixture do not produce the same record.

There is also a narrower correctness point worth separating, because it is true independently of any test. A resolver should only read an environment variable belonging to the harness whose descriptor matched. AI_AGENT is a shared name that several harnesses write, so the codex descriptor reading it means a codex actor can inherit a value written by a different tool entirely. The classifier compounds this by treating mere presence of the variable as evidence that the resolver had valid input, which is what turns an honest unavailable into a misleading failed. A record that says a resolver failed, when in fact it was handed another harness's value, states something untrue about the run.

A sandboxed workspace neutralizes harness signal environment, so recorded provenance depends only on the harness the fixture declares and never on the process running the suite; A provenance resolver reads only environment variables belonging to the harness whose descriptor matched, so a codex descriptor never consumes a value written by another tool; The outcome classifier distinguishes a resolver that was handed valid input and failed from one that was handed another harness's value, so the record never reports resolver_failed for input that was never the harness's to begin with; The agent-runtime-primitives expectation holds with AI_AGENT unset, set to a value carrying a parseable version, and set to a value that does not, proving the verdict no longer varies with the host; Local preflight carries a control that sets a foreign harness variable and fails if any spec's verdict changes, so this divergence class cannot silently return

author: harness:claude-code
message: Wire the host-provenance leak into the identity lineage, the reproducibility precedent, and the outcome ladder

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Reproduction, exact and cheap, recorded 2026-08-09 at commit 9a0a048b6. Filed only; not fixed in this pass.

Failing run, with the harness variable present as an agent would have it:

  node scripts/run-tests.mjs test -- tests/unit/sdk/agent-runtime-primitives.spec.ts

fails one of sixteen, at agent-runtime-primitives.spec.ts:741, on attributes update and close mutations to the detected harness. Both compared history entries carry an unexpected context.agent_provenance_outcomes.version block reading status failed, reason resolver_failed, resolver ai_agent_version, rule_version v1.

Passing run, identical in every other respect:

  env -u AI_AGENT node scripts/run-tests.mjs test -- tests/unit/sdk/agent-runtime-primitives.spec.ts

passes sixteen of sixteen. One variable is the entire difference, and it is a variable the fixture never sets and never refers to.

The host value on this machine is claude-code_2-1-226_agent. It matters that this string is not malformed: the resolver's regex requires the version at the end of the string, and this value ends in the literal text agent, so a perfectly ordinary harness value fails to parse. An agent whose AI_AGENT happened to end in a version would produce a third outcome again, which is why the acceptance criteria ask for all three forms to be exercised rather than only the unset case.

Chain of custody through the source, so the fix has three separable candidate sites rather than one guess. src/core/shared/author.ts:219 declares the codex descriptor's version resolver as ai_agent_version. src/core/shared/author.ts:569 implements that resolver by reading env.AI_AGENT, a name several harnesses write, with no check that the value belongs to the harness that matched. src/core/shared/author.ts:897 classifies the outcome, and decides between failed and unavailable by asking only whether env.AI_AGENT is non-blank; presence of any value is taken as evidence that the resolver had legitimate input, which is what converts an honest unavailable into a misleading failed.

Confirmation that this is not a flake and not caused by the change shipped alongside it. The failure appeared first inside a full coverage run and then reproduced identically in isolation, and it reproduces on every invocation with the variable set. Two other specs failed in that same coverage run, governance-read-performance and surface-replication-gate, and both pass cleanly when re-run without concurrent load; those two are wall-clock sensitive and are not this. Continuous integration is green at this commit, which is consistent with hosted runners setting no AI_AGENT.

Scope note on what this does and does not touch. The two history entries are otherwise correct: author is harness:codex, author_source is detected, and the patch contents are as expected. The leak affects the provenance outcome block only. That is what makes it a containment question rather than a correctness question about detection, and it is why the item is parented on continuous integration rather than on the identity lineage, while still citing that lineage.
